whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the B2B Commerce Developer AP exam for?

personas.label: Developers building custom storefronts
personas.description: You build Lightning Web Components and Apex for B2B stores and want to show you know the commerce extension points.

personas.label: Integration engineers
personas.description: You connect B2B stores to ERPs and outside services for pricing, stock, tax and shipping.

personas.label: Technical consultants
personas.description: You advise clients on what can be configured and what needs custom development in B2B Commerce.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the B2B Commerce Developer AP Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: It is a technical exam. You need to know where B2B Commerce lets you plug in your own code, how storefront components work, and how the APIs are used. The pass mark is moderate, but the questions go deep.
bullets: About 65% to pass, roughly 39 correct answers. Check the official guide for the current figure.
Extension points. Expect questions on custom pricing, inventory, shipping and tax integrations, and how to plug them into checkout.
LWC and APIs. Building and customising store components and calling the Commerce APIs come up often.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: People who have built at least one custom component or integration for a B2B store do best. Before you book. Aim for 80% or more on practice tests.

examFormat.heading: B2B Commerce Developer AP Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: Accredited Professional exams are taken online. Here is what to expect:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Most questions describe a business need that standard features don't cover, such as prices from an ERP or a custom product page, and ask for the right way to build it.
bestWayToPass: Learn the extension points: Know how custom pricing, inventory, shipping and tax logic plugs into the store and checkout.
Build an LWC for a store: Know how to expose it in Experience Builder and get data with the Commerce APIs.
Know when not to code: If configuration can meet the need, that is usually the right answer.
Understand search and data: How products are indexed, which fields are searchable, and when to rebuild the index.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how you extend B2B Commerce with code: custom storefront components, Apex integrations for pricing, stock, shipping and tax, and the Commerce APIs. The exam is 60 scored questions in 75 minutes, with a 68% pass mark, weighted towards Advanced Lightning Web Component Development (30%) and Basic Lightning Web Component Development (20%).

keyConcepts.h2: B2B Commerce Developer AP: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: LWC Commerce Components & Override Pattern
blocks.body: B2B stores are built in Experience Builder from Lightning Web Components. You can add your own LWCs to store pages, or replace a standard component when it doesn't do what you need. To make a component usable in the builder, expose it with the right targets in its metadata file and add properties admins can set. Store components get context, such as the current product, cart or buyer account, from commerce modules and wire adapters, so they show the right data for the logged-in buyer. Keep components small and reuse standard ones where you can.

blocks.heading: Commerce APIs & Storefront REST APIs
blocks.body: The **Commerce Connect REST APIs** (often called the B2B Commerce APIs) let you work with products, carts, checkout, wishlists and orders from code or outside apps. Apex also has **ConnectApi** classes for the same tasks from server-side code. Use them instead of querying and updating commerce objects directly, because the APIs apply entitlements and pricing rules for the buyer. Headless and mobile apps can use the same APIs to offer the store outside the website.

blocks.heading: Checkout Integrations & Tax/Payment
blocks.body: Checkout can call outside systems for **inventory**, **pricing**, **shipping** and **tax**. You write an Apex class that implements the right integration interface (or a commerce extension), register it, and link it to the store. Payment uses a **payment gateway adapter** that talks to the payment provider, so card data never sits in Salesforce. Integrations should handle slow or failed responses cleanly and return clear messages to the buyer. Test them with realistic carts and failure cases.

blocks.heading: Search Configuration & Merchandising
blocks.body: Store search is driven by a **search index** built from products, categories and their fields. Admins choose which fields are searchable and which ones become filters (facets). Developers may add custom fields to products and make them searchable. After changing these settings or loading many products, the index must be **rebuilt**, and large catalogs should be rebuilt outside busy hours. Product data loaded by integrations must include the fields search relies on.

blocks.heading: Testing, Deployment & Performance
blocks.body: Apex for commerce needs test classes like any other Apex, with 75% coverage to deploy. Mock outside callouts in tests so they don't depend on live systems. Store setup lives partly in metadata and partly in data, so plan how to move catalogs, buyer groups and settings between orgs. For performance, avoid heavy work in components that load on every page, cache data that doesn't change often, and keep integration calls fast, since slow pricing or tax calls make checkout slow.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce B2B Commerce Developer Accredited Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Most questions start with a need that standard setup can't meet. Pick the supported extension point, not a workaround.

blocks.heading: B2B Commerce Extensibility Framework
blocks.body: Custom pricing, stock, shipping and tax all plug in through supported integration points registered to the store. Don't rebuild checkout from scratch.

blocks.heading: Storefront LWC Development
blocks.body: Expose components to Experience Builder in the metadata file, and get store context from commerce modules rather than hard-coding IDs.

blocks.heading: Apex Extension Points
blocks.body: Use ConnectApi commerce classes in Apex so entitlements and prices are applied for the buyer.

blocks.heading: External Catalog Integration
blocks.body: Load products from outside systems with external IDs, then rebuild the search index.

blocks.heading: Order Fulfillment Integration
blocks.body: Send placed orders to the ERP with events or async Apex, and keep order status in sync.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications After This AP
nextCertsAfter.intro: Good next steps after B2B Commerce Developer:

sampleQuestions.question: Prices for some customers must come from the company's ERP at the moment a product is added to the cart. What is the right approach?
options: Write an Apex pricing integration and register it with the store
Change the store theme
Ask buyers to phone for prices
Copy all ERP prices into product descriptions
sampleQuestions.explanation: B2B Commerce lets you plug in a custom pricing integration so prices are fetched from the ERP when needed.
whyWrong: The theme doesn't affect pricing.
Phoning for prices defeats the purpose of the store.
Prices in descriptions can't be used by the cart.

sampleQuestions.question: A developer builds an LWC that should appear in Experience Builder for admins to drag onto store pages. What must they do?
options: Add it to a page layout
Write it in Visualforce instead
Expose the component and add the right targets in its metadata file
Deploy it as a static resource only
sampleQuestions.explanation: LWCs need to be exposed with community or Lightning targets in their js-meta.xml file to show up in Experience Builder.
whyWrong: Page layouts are for internal record pages.
Visualforce isn't used for B2B store pages.
A static resource isn't a component.

sampleQuestions.question: An Apex class needs to add a product to a buyer's cart while respecting their entitlements and prices. What should it use?
options: A direct DML insert on CartItem
The ConnectApi commerce classes
An outbound message
A SOQL query on Product2 only
sampleQuestions.explanation: ConnectApi commerce methods apply the buyer's entitlements and pricing rules, which direct DML would skip.
whyWrong: Direct DML skips the commerce rules and can create invalid carts.
Outbound messages send data out of Salesforce.
A query reads data but doesn't add to a cart.

sampleQuestions.question: Tax must be calculated by an outside tax service during checkout. What should the developer build?
options: A tax integration class registered with the store
A report that shows tax
A validation rule
A formula field on the cart
sampleQuestions.explanation: Checkout supports a tax integration point. A registered Apex class can call the tax service and return the tax lines.
whyWrong: Reports show data after the fact.
Validation rules block saves, they don't calculate tax.
Formula fields can't call outside services.

sampleQuestions.question: Card payments must be processed by a payment provider without storing card numbers in Salesforce. What should be used?
options: A custom text field for card numbers
Emailing card details to finance
A payment gateway adapter for the provider
A long text area on the Order
sampleQuestions.explanation: A payment gateway adapter connects checkout to the provider, which handles the card data and returns a result.
whyWrong: Storing card numbers in fields is a serious security risk.
Email is insecure for card data.
Any field that stores card numbers is a risk.

sampleQuestions.question: A custom product field should be searchable in the store. The developer has created the field. What else must happen?
options: Put the field value in the product name
Add the field to the buyer's profile
Nothing, all fields are searched automatically
Mark the field as searchable in search settings and rebuild the search index
sampleQuestions.explanation: Only fields chosen in search settings are indexed, and the index must be rebuilt to include them.
whyWrong: Changing names is a workaround that breaks data quality.
Profiles don't control store search.
Fields are not searched unless chosen.

sampleQuestions.question: A pricing integration sometimes takes 20 seconds to respond, making checkout slow. What should the developer do first?
options: Remove pricing from checkout
Add a timeout and a clear fallback message, and work with the ERP team to speed up the service
Retry the call ten times in a row
Ask buyers to wait
sampleQuestions.explanation: Integrations should fail cleanly with timeouts and helpful messages, and the slow service itself needs fixing.
whyWrong: Removing pricing breaks the order.
Ten retries make checkout even slower.
Asking buyers to wait leads to abandoned carts.

sampleQuestions.question: A mobile app needs to let buyers browse products and manage their cart using the same rules as the website. What should it use?
options: Screen scraping of the website
Direct SOQL from the mobile app
A nightly CSV export
The B2B Commerce REST APIs
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Commerce REST APIs give the app the same products, prices and cart logic as the store.
whyWrong: Screen scraping is fragile and breaks when the site changes.
Mobile apps can't run SOQL directly, and it would skip commerce rules.
A nightly file can't manage a live cart.

sampleQuestions.question: Test classes for a shipping integration fail when the shipping provider is down. What should be changed?
options: Lower the coverage target
Run tests only at night
Use HttpCalloutMock so tests don't call the live service
Remove the tests
sampleQuestions.explanation: Mock callouts let tests run the integration code without depending on outside systems.
whyWrong: Coverage requirements are fixed.
The provider can be down at night too.
Removing tests stops deployments, which need 75% coverage.

sampleQuestions.question: A business wants a product comparison feature that no standard component offers. What should the developer do?
options: Use a Visualforce page in the store
Build a custom LWC and add it to the product pages in Experience Builder
Edit Salesforce's standard component source
Ask buyers to open two tabs
sampleQuestions.explanation: Custom LWCs are the supported way to add new features to store pages.
whyWrong: Visualforce doesn't fit modern store pages.
You can't edit Salesforce's standard component code.
Two tabs is not a feature.

sampleQuestions.question: 10,000 products are loaded from the ERP each night. Buyers say new products don't show up in search until days later. What is the fix?
options: Load the products one at a time
Rebuild the search index after each nightly load
Turn off search
Make the product names shorter
sampleQuestions.explanation: New products only appear in search once the index is rebuilt, so the rebuild should follow the load.
whyWrong: Loading one at a time doesn't update the index.
Turning off search makes the store unusable.
Name length isn't the problem.

sampleQuestions.question: When an order is placed, it must be sent to the ERP without slowing down the buyer's checkout. What fits best?
options: Asking sales reps to re-enter the order
A synchronous callout before the order is saved
A nightly manual export
Publish an event or start async Apex after the order is created
sampleQuestions.explanation: Async processing sends the order in the background, so the buyer isn't kept waiting.
whyWrong: Re-entering orders is slow and error-prone.
A synchronous call makes the buyer wait and fails if the ERP is down.
Nightly exports delay fulfilment.

sampleQuestions.question: Store components should show data for the logged-in buyer's account. How should a component find the current account?
options: Use the store's commerce context rather than hard-coding an account ID
Read it from a custom setting
Ask the buyer to type their account number
Hard-code the account ID in the component
sampleQuestions.explanation: Commerce context modules give the component the current buyer account, cart and store at run time.
whyWrong: A custom setting holds one value for everyone.
Buyers shouldn't have to type their account.
A hard-coded ID would show the same account to every buyer.

sampleQuestions.question: Before deploying a custom inventory integration to production, what must the Apex code have?
options: A managed package
A Visualforce page
Test classes giving at least 75% code coverage
A Full sandbox refresh
sampleQuestions.explanation: All Apex needs tests with at least 75% coverage to deploy to production.
whyWrong: Packaging isn't required for a custom class.
Visualforce isn't required.
A refresh isn't a deployment requirement.

sampleQuestions.question: A requirement can be met either by configuring a standard checkout option or by writing custom code. What should the developer recommend?
options: Use the standard configuration
Always write custom code
Build a separate checkout outside Salesforce
Ignore the requirement
sampleQuestions.explanation: Configuration is cheaper to maintain and upgrade. Code is for needs that configuration can't meet.
whyWrong: Custom code adds cost and upgrade risk when it isn't needed.
A separate checkout loses the built-in commerce rules.
Ignoring requirements isn't an option.
